skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-google-ads-enhanced-conversions
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up or troubleshoot Google Ads Enhanced Conversions for WooCommerce. Check server-side tracking, configure checkout consent, review Google's customer data terms, and verify delivery with a paid test order.
skill.summary: Configure and verify Google Ads Enhanced Conversions for WooCommerce with Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts concern Markdown syntax, documentation links, or routine setup checks. Three alerts reflect real risks: an unpinned installer, authenticated order retrieval, and a remote MCP tool with write access. The review also found gaps in credential handling, setup scope, and trust checks for remote content, but no evidence of prompt injection.

remediation.issue: The installation example does not pin the installer or skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin both the installer version and skill commit. Require explicit approval before running the installer.

remediation.issue: The verification workflow can fetch live orders, and the remote MCP interface can perform writes.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the workspace and storefront with the user. Use delivery status or a designated test order instead of listing recent orders. Restrict MCP to the required actions and confirm any write before execution.

remediation.issue: The shared secret-handling rule allows credentials for unrelated platforms to pass through the assistant.
remediation.suggestion: Remove these exceptions from the WooCommerce Google Ads skill. Keep credential entry in the provider's authenticated interface and do not pass secrets through chat or command arguments.

remediation.issue: The fallback setup includes an initial order import and mentions ad channels outside the requested scope.
remediation.suggestion: Limit prerequisite steps to Google Ads. Explain what Product Metrics imports and obtain separate approval before importing order history or connecting another channel.

remediation.issue: The fallback treats mutable web documentation as equivalent to the reviewed local instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed references or verify a pinned copy. Treat fetched text as untrusted and do not let it expand allowed tools, destinations, or actions.

remediation.issue: Browser handoffs do not specify how to validate returned URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Validate HTTPS hosts and redirect destinations against the expected provider before presenting a link. Use the provider's known dashboard when verification fails.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Handling Outside the Skill Scope
semantic_findings.description: The secret-handling rule lets the assistant accept Lightspeed, Meta, and OpenAI credentials and pass them to a command. None is required for this Google Ads workflow. Handling these secrets through the assistant can expose them in chat or tool traces.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rule explicitly exempts three unrelated integrations from its normal prohibition on asking for secrets. No evidence shows that any credential was collected.

semantic_findings.title: Prerequisite Setup Can Exceed Google Ads Scope
semantic_findings.description: The fallback store guide instructs the merchant to send initial orders and lists Meta and ChatGPT Ads alongside Google Ads. It does not require separate approval for the historical import or limit channel setup to the requested destination.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback queues an order import before the guide reaches consent configuration and lists channels outside the main workflow. The reference does not show that any import or channel connection occurred.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Documentation Can Change the Workflow
semantic_findings.description: If local references are missing, the skill treats current vendor Markdown as equivalent setup instructions. A changed or compromised page could introduce actions or destinations outside the reviewed workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback expressly directs the assistant to substitute unversioned web content for local instructions. No evidence of compromise or injection was found in the reviewed files.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Handoff Lacks Destination Validation
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the assistant to present a service-provided browser URL as the next user step. It does not require checking the destination before directing the merchant to a possible sign-in or consent page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The browser handoff rule specifies no host or redirect check. The risk depends on control of the returned URL, and no malicious URL was observed.

content.user_title: Set Up Google Ads Enhanced Conversions for WooCommerce
content.value_statement: Google Ads may miss purchases when cookies alone cannot connect them to ad clicks. Use Product Metrics to configure consent-based matching and verify paid order delivery.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP and identify unfinished steps.
Check whether the WooCommerce connection and Google Ads conversion actions are ready for Enhanced Conversions.
Guide merchants through consent banner configuration and explain which consent choice controls each type of data.
Explain how to review Google's customer data terms and recheck Data Manager acceptance.
Guide a paid WooCommerce test order and help interpret the live delivery status.
limitations: This workflow requires Product Metrics Pro and active server-side conversion tracking to Google Ads.
A person must perform WordPress admin steps, accept Google's terms, and make any changes to primary conversion actions.
A verified test order confirms live delivery. It does not prove Google matched it to an ad click.
Customer Match, campaign bidding, and initial conversion tracking setup are separate workflows.

use_cases.title: Check Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Identify what remains before using checkout data for Google Ads Enhanced Conversions.

use_cases.title: Resolve Data Manager Rejection
use_cases.description: Find where to review customer data terms and recheck acceptance without changing campaign bidding.

use_cases.title: Verify a Paid Test Order
use_cases.description: Validate live order delivery after a consent banner change without reviewing unrelated customer orders.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Prerequisites
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Learn what the setup requires.
prompt_templates.prompt: List the accounts, access, and WooCommerce settings I need for Google Ads Enhanced Conversions through Product Metrics. Do not connect to my accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Check Current Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Read Product Metrics setup status for the store and Google Ads account I confirm. List unfinished steps without changing settings or reading live customer orders.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Rejected Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Data Manager acceptance says Rejected. Explain what I should check in Google Ads, including whether my manager account controls the terms. Leave conversion actions unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Consent and Delivery Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Validate a consent configuration change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan paid test orders for my supported consent banner. Compare expected behavior for ad user data, ad storage only, and neither. Separate live delivery from Google Ads matching.

output_examples.input: Product Metrics shows Action required, and it says another account manages the terms.
output: Open the Google Ads manager account shown in Product Metrics and review the customer data terms there.
Return to Tracking, open Google Ads, and select Re-check under Enhanced conversions.
Confirm the status reads Ready before testing delivery.

output_examples.input: I selected my consent banner. How do I verify store delivery?
output: Clear the full-page cache and confirm Configure consent shows the banner visitors see.
In WooCommerce, open Product Metrics and select Verify with next paid order.
Pay for a test order within ten minutes, then select Refresh connection status.
Verified confirms live delivery. It does not confirm Google matched the order to an ad click.

best_practices: Confirm the store and Google Ads client account before checking status or requesting changes.
Clear the full-page cache after configuring the banner, and test the consent choices with dedicated test orders.
Keep Product Metrics actions secondary unless the account owner explicitly changes what campaigns optimize for.
anti_patterns: Pasting a WooCommerce setup token, API key, or customer billing details into chat.
Treating ad storage consent as permission to send hashed billing identifiers.
Assuming that a Verified delivery status proves Google matched the order to an ad click.

faq.question: Do I need Google Tag Manager?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics sends the data server-side through Google's Data Manager without adding a Google tag.

faq.question: Which consent banners are supported?
faq.answer: The guide lists OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, and Osano. Clear the full-page cache after selecting the banner.

faq.question: Which billing fields are hashed?
faq.answer: Product Metrics hashes billing email, phone, and names with SHA-256. When a complete name set is sent, country and postcode remain unhashed.

faq.question: What happens if a visitor declines ad user data?
faq.answer: If the visitor allows ad storage, Google Ads can still receive the order without hashed customer data. If the visitor allows neither, the order is not sent.

faq.question: Who can accept Google's customer data terms?
faq.answer: A Google Ads administrator must accept the terms. Use the manager account if Product Metrics says it manages those terms.

faq.question: Why is the status still Setting up?
faq.answer: Data Manager can take about 15 minutes to recognize new conversion actions. Select Re-check in Product Metrics afterward.
